_note: The visual fallback for sources that block automated fetching. Counts come from the real project: the blocked/failed fetch outcomes logged across the corpus, the screenshots kept as evidence, and the two protocols wired to fall back. No URL, page or captured content is included.

_provenance.produced_by: the corpus source logs + the project's browser tool and phase plan

the_problem.symptom: the professional-network source returns HTTP 999 to automated fetches
the_problem.also_affected: pages that render their content with JavaScript, and pages that only reveal data after scrolling or clicking
the_problem.why_it_hurt_here: those are the sources for protocol 04 (who works in administration) and protocol 08 (how to reach them) - the two protocols the whole prospecting exercise exists for

the_fix.approach: drive a real browser (Playwright) and capture a screenshot, then read the image directly with the model's vision capability instead of parsing HTML
the_fix.headless_note: headless Chromium is detectable by the blocking site; the tool can run headed when it is

the_limit.what_it_does_not_change: the anti-hallucination contract still applies - a profile seen in a screenshot is a verified sighting, a profile guessed from a name is not
the_limit.residual: 84 blocked or failed fetches remain in the corpus; the fallback is manual and per-source, not automatic
the_limit.not_measured: there is no before/after experiment - the fix predates the bulk of the corpus, so no controlled comparison exists
